what: Air Products makes industrial gases: oxygen, nitrogen, hydrogen and argon. It builds plants next to customers' refineries and factories and supplies them under contracts that run for fifteen or twenty years.
customers: Refiners, chemical producers, steelmakers, electronics manufacturers, food processors and hospitals.
money: on-site gas supply, pipelines and merchant gas
industrial gases for electronics and heavy industry
moat: On-site plants built inside customer sites under long contracts with take-or-pay terms, which makes switching supplier effectively impossible.
risks: It took large write-downs on hydrogen and clean energy projects, which pushed reported operating profit negative
Several green hydrogen projects were cancelled after costs rose
Debt of about $18 billion funded that programme
New management is still resetting the capital plan
opportunities: The core industrial gas business remains contracted and steady under long agreements
Cancelling weak projects frees capital and should restore returns
Electronics and semiconductor fabs need large volumes of ultra-pure gases
watch: Capital spending discipline and whether returns on new projects recover toward the level Linde earns.
